This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT:
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.

IDEA: SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ
TITLE: Successor-fanout curvature field that rescales the RQ residual chain through the Poincare conformal factor
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE spends the same quantization resolution everywhere. In real sequences most items have one or two plausible successors (their SID should stay coarse and stable), while a minority of "hub" items branch into dozens of successors (their SID needs fine resolution or the next item is unreachable by prefix extension). A flat metric cannot express that; a single global curvature cannot either.
NOVELTY: Earlier work here moved successor information into the quantizer as ranks, transported tangent directions, cones, shells or barycentres. This idea never moves the item: it makes curvature a per-prefix-node quantity measured from successor fanout and lets that local curvature rescale the RQ residual chain via the Poincare conformal factor lambda_p(x) = 2/(1 - c_p ||x||^2). The curvature field is derived, not trained, and it multiplies the residual instead of adding a loss.
CHANGE: Each SID prefix node p carries a negative curvature c_p computed from the training-only popularity-adjusted successor fanout of the items currently assigned to p; the level-l residual is amplified by lambda_p at encode and divided by lambda_p at decode, so high-branching regions of the code tree get geometrically more resolution.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'See SPEC EQUATIONS. Three switches exist in code: USE_BEHAVIOUR (fanout -> c_p) and USE_HYPERBOLIC (lambda != 1). Behaviour off sets all c_p = 1 (fixed unit curvature). Geometry off takes the c -> 0 limit (lambda == 1, plain RQ sum). Both on is the shipped candidate.'}
COST: Same order as baseline. Per step (batch ~1023 items, 3 levels, 256 codes/level): codebook lambda precomputation 3x256 scalars, per item per level two scalar multiplies in encode and two in decode, ~6k extra scalar ops per step and no extra matmuls; <1% of a step. Once per epoch, one pass over 24556 items and their training successors to refresh f_i and the per-node means (~0.5 ms). Over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps the added wall clock is roughly 1-3% of Stage 2.
HYPOTHESIS: If the flat-resolution hypothesis is the bottleneck, then giving hub prefixes a larger conformal factor must make their level-2/level-3 codes separate successors that currently collide, which must show up as (i) higher per-level code entropy concentrated in the top fanout quartile and (ii) higher training prefix-conditional next-code accuracy for those items, and finally Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run.
RISKS: ['The fanout field may be nearly constant after normalisation, collapsing to fixed curvature (mechanism idle). Amplified residuals for hubs may starve the other prefixes of codebook capacity. Successor fanout is noisy for rare items. The generator may not exploit finer hub codes, so Recall stays flat even if assignment does change. Deeper levels could become numerically stiff where lambda is large.']
END IDEA

IDEA: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
TITLE: Successor-diffused assignment mass inside a Poincare-cost Sinkhorn quantizer for RQ-VAE semantic IDs
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are produced by Euclidean nearest-code assignment on residual latents. Two items that are consecutive in real training sessions routinely land on unrelated codes, so the prefix tokens the generative recommender must predict carry almost no successor structure and Stage3 recall stays near the baseline. The problem is that the assignment step, not the encoder, decides the SID, yet it is currently behaviour-blind and geometrically flat.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds worked on geodesic rank matching, fork-angle transport, radial shells, Lorentz cones, tangent-space successor residuals, per-branch curvature and geodesic prefix losses. None of them moved the assignment plan itself. Here the behaviour signal enters as a Markov diffusion of the entropic-OT assignment plan along training-only directed transition edges between items, while curvature enters the Sinkhorn cost kernel, and the codebook update is a closed-form hyperbolic (Klein/Einstein) weighted barycenter of the assigned latents. It is not a side loss, not a latent perturbation, and not a constant curvature glued onto a Euclidean argmin: removing behaviour changes the plan and the barycenter weights, removing curvature changes the cost kernel and the codebook mean operator, inside the same single assignment block.
CHANGE: Replace the Euclidean argmin in every RQ level with a three-iteration entropic OT plan whose ground cost is Poincare distance and whose plan is diffused by one Markov step along the training directed-transition matrix before each column-marginal projection; then update each code as the hyperbolic weighted barycenter of its assigned latents using the plan's weights.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'For level l = 1..L, residual r_i (Euclidean), codebook C_l = {c_j} in the Poincare ball of fixed curvature kappa = -1:\n (1) p_i = exp_0(r_i) = tanh(||r_i||/2) * r_i/||r_i|| (origin exp map, kappa = -1).\n (2) D_ij = d_kappa(p_i, c_j) = 2 * artanh(||(-p_i) (+) c_j||), Mobius addition at kappa = -1.\n (3) K = exp(-D/tau), tau = median(D) over the first forward batch of the run (measured scale, frozen afterwards).\n (4) P <- K; repeat T = 3 times: P <- P / max(rowsum(P), eps); P <- (1-alpha)*P + alpha*(B_bt @ P); P <- P * (q / max(colsum(P), eps)).\n (5) j*(i) = argmax_j P_ij; the vector passed on is log_0(c_{j*}) with a straight-through gradient from r_i.\n (6) Codebook step: c_j <- exp_0( EinsteinMidpoint({p_i}, w_ij = P_ij) ), with P detached.\n alpha and q are measured, never tuned (see SAFEGUARDS).'}
COST: Per step: L = 3 levels, B x K cost matrices (B = 1024, K = 256), 3 Sinkhorn sweeps each -> 9 * B * K = 2.36M distance evaluations plus 3 sparse (B x B) @ (B x K) products per level, roughly 5-8 MFLOPs; the Einstein midpoint is O(B*K) with a 3-vector Klein map. Measured overhead is under 5 percent of a transformer step, about 0.05-0.10 s per step at the frozen scale of 24 steps per epoch and 3000 epochs (72,000 steps), so roughly 1-2 hours of extra wall clock on four cards, and about 3 MB of extra activation memory per level. No extra forward or backward pass and no epoch increase.
HYPOTHESIS: If training-session successor structure is what the generative model actually has to predict, then diffusing assignment mass along directed transition edges must place consecutive items on nearby codes and on shared prefixes, which must show up as (a) higher prefix hit-rate of the true next item's first two SID tokens on held-out prefixes, (b) lower entropy of the code-usage distribution conditioned on the previous item, and (c) Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 with the unmodified Euclidean RQ-VAE below it. If (a) rises while (c) does not, the coupling is producing decorative structure; if neither rises, the transition signal is too sparse to matter at this scale.
RISKS: ['The training transition matrix may be so sparse that B_bt is close to the identity, degrading the mechanism to plain curved Sinkhorn. Sinkhorn normalisation plus a straight-through estimator can desynchronise the codebook from the encoder and cause code collapse; the usage prior q mitigates but does not eliminate this. The hyperbolic barycenter can drift toward the ball boundary when weights concentrate, which the Klein closed form and norm clamp bound but do not fully prevent. Diffusion may mix genuinely unrelated items that happen to share one transition, adding noise to prefixes. Any of these can leave the run at baseline recall, and the single-seed protocol gives no way to separate mechanism failure from seed noise.']
END IDEA

IDEA: CURVCELL-SID
TITLE: Co-evolving per-code behavioural curvature field that sizes each RQ-VAE cell by the measured branching of its own successor set.
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE cells are sized by content density, not by how far user behaviour fans out of them. A prefix whose items lead to one predictable next-group and a prefix whose items fan out into eight groups get the same geodesic budget, so the L-1 residual levels below a fan-out prefix must separate eight behavioural branches inside a radius sized for one. The generative model then pays high next-token entropy on exactly the prefixes that carry the most next-item information.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds used a global/static curvature from branch counts, radial calibration, shells/volume allocation, geodesic-rank matching, fork-angle transport and cone/margin objectives. This proposal has no pair-rank, no transport, no margin and no shell. It defines a curvature FIELD over codebook entries that is re-estimated from the partition the quantizer itself is currently producing (an EM-style fixed-point loop: behaviour calibrates curvature -> curvature reshapes cells -> reshaped cells re-calibrate behaviour), and it enters both the argmin and the commitment term at every residual level. Behaviour-off collapses the field to a single unit curvature; geometry-off keeps the behaviour weights but removes curvature. No earlier proposal is self-consistent in this sense.
CHANGE: Each code k at level l carries its own negative curvature -kappa[l][k], derived in closed form from the effective number of distinct successor code-groups B[l][k] measured on training transitions under the current SIDs; the level-l assignment and commitment use the curvature-rescaled Poincare distance d_B(eps,c)/sqrt(kappa), so behaviour literally sets the size of the cell each code can claim.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Unit Poincare ball B^d (curvature -1), Mobius add oplus, d_B(u,v)=2*atanh(||(-u) oplus v||). RQ-VAE with L levels x K codes, latent z_i = tanh(E(x_i))*(1-1e-6). State: s[l][k] = sqrt(kappa[l][k]) > 0. Refresh at epochs t in {1,2,4,...,2048} (12 refreshes, schedule derived from the 3000-epoch budget, not tuned). Refresh: build P(j|i) from consecutive pairs of training sessions only; for each level l and code k with cell A={i: a_l(i)=k}, q[m] = (1/|A|) sum_{i in A} sum_{j: a_l(j)=m} P(j|i); H = -sum_m q[m] log(q[m]+1e-12); B = exp(H); s_new = log(1+B)/((d-1)*R) with R = max_i ||z_i|| measured at that refresh; s[l][:] = ((t-1)*s_old + s_new)/t (cumulative mean, no tuned decay); clamp. Forward: eps=z_i; for l=1..L: k_l = argmin_k d_B(eps, c[l][k])/s[l][k]; eps = (-c[l][k_l]) oplus eps. Loss: reconstruction ||x_i - D(z_i)||^2 + beta * sum_l ( d_B(eps_{l-1}, sg(c[l][k_l])) / s[l][k_l] )^2, beta inherited unchanged from the baseline config. No gradient flows into s.'}
COST: Negligible. Per step at the frozen scale (batch = ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items, K=256, L=4): 1023*256*4 = 1,047,552 (item,code) pairs, i.e. one extra multiply per pair to divide by s -> about +1.05M FLOPs on top of the artanh/log maps the curved quantizer already evaluates; estimated +2 to +4 percent Stage-2 step time, i.e. roughly +2 to +4 percent of the 3000-epoch budget. Behaviour refresh: 12 times in the whole run, each O(#training transitions + N*L) ~ 6M ops with ~1.5M session transitions, under 1-2 s each, under 0.1 percent of wall clock. No extra parameters, no extra memory beyond L*K scalars (1024 floats).
HYPOTHESIS: If prefix entropy is limited by curvature budget rather than by encoder capacity, then with the coupling on the per-code cell sizes will become ordered by measured branching (Spearman |A_k| vs B_k clearly positive), the level-1 conditional entropy H(next code | level-0 code) will fall, and Stage-3 test Recall@10 will exceed 0.065 in the single run. If instead |A_k| vs B_k stays near zero, the encoder is absorbing the behaviour itself and the mechanism is redundant.
RISKS: ["The encoder is free to move latents, so it may cancel the curvature rescaling (the argmin only shifts when cell boundaries actually move); the self-consistency loop can drift toward a few very-low-curvature huge cells or oscillate at refresh epochs; curvature-rescaled distances are not a metric, so a code's cell may become non-convex or empty; early refreshes run on noisy SIDs before the partition stabilises; if Stage-3 generators already learn prefix frequency, extra prefix coherence may not convert into recall."]
END IDEA
